steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Global media refers to media products and companies that operate across national boundaries, distributing content to worldwide audiences. | Key Fact: Cultural imperialism: the theory that Western (particularly American) media dominates global markets, overwhelming local cultures and imposing Western values. Hollywood films and American TV are distributed worldwide. | Key Fact: Glocalisation: global media products are adapted for local markets — e.g. McDonald's menus varying by country, or Netflix commissioning local-language content (Squid Game, Money Heist). | Key Fact: Transnational media companies: corporations that operate across multiple countries — e.g. Disney, Netflix, Sony. They produce and distribute content globally, but adapt strategies for local markets.
